items.html:
Implemented upstream illumination benchmarks in benchmark_illumination.py:

  • treams-full: public full interacting T-matrix followed by requested illumination.
  • treams-selected: clearly labeled custom upstream workflow using public interaction assembly plus SciPy LU and selected right-hand sides.
  • Both use separate forward-only workers without importing Rust. Native forward/adjoint measurements remain intact.
  • --oracle-limit now controls actual upstream timing and comparison; default 768. Raise explicitly for larger comparisons.
  • Existing timing/RSS schema retained; added workflow labels and upstream package fingerprint.

Verified Ruff and all five metadata tests, including an import-isolation assertion. Eight-row end-to-end smoke passed: upstream error 2.21e-15, largest native comparison error 1.22e-10. No rebuild, commits, or push.

Audit findings:

  • The 527-case manifest covers 188 workload names, but lacks fresh macro measurements for uniform clusters, spherical fields, periodic spheres/arrays, slabs, rotations, conversions, and plane-field operators.
  • Most expensive historical cases: cylindrical 2D lattice sums at 4,096 samples (~29.5 seconds per upstream evaluation), cylindrical periodic expansion at 16 particles (~17.2 seconds), spherical 3D lattice sums at 4,096 samples (~11.1 seconds). Full historical run took 73m53s.
  • Unsuffixed macro cases record native adjoints; -forward/-public cases generally measure forward-only APIs. slab has public forward timing and separate recorded reverse timing.
  • particle-cluster-public alternates multipole orders L and L+1; local coefficients are prepared outside timing. Uniform cluster includes local coefficient construction. Label these separately.
  • Field contraction avoids allocating the full operator; keep weighted-field versus complete-operator comparisons explicit.
  • EBCM timing uses the legacy surface integral for identical mathematics. Keep strict comparisons at L=3,4; known cancellation prevents an honest generic L=6 speedup claim.
  • Peak RSS includes imports and allocator retention; also show baseline RSS. Tiny-kernel RSS ratios mainly reflect package import costs.
  • Reverse timings are native-only; upstream has no matching analytic reverse API.

Useful fresh illumination grid:

# Comparable native/full upstream workload; increase the cap deliberately.
python scripts/benchmark_illumination.py \
  --particles 512 --lmax 1 --columns 1 --threads 4 \
  --dense-limit 3072 --oracle-limit 3072 --repeats 3 \
  --output benchmarks/results/illumination-n512-l1-p1.json

# Very large native capacity, with explicitly absent same-size dense comparison.
python scripts/benchmark_illumination.py \
  --particles 2048 --lmax 1 --columns 1 --threads 4 \
  --dense-limit 3072 --oracle-limit 768 --repeats 3 \
  --output benchmarks/results/illumination-n2048-l1-p1.json

Historical matrix-free N=1024,L=1,P=1: forward 2.19s, reverse 2.83s, peak 47.9MiB. Quadratic extrapolation suggests N=2048 ≈9s per forward and ≈3 minutes for the full benchmark; N=4096 ≈35s and ≈13 minutes, provided iteration counts stay comparable. These are planning estimates, not measurements.

GPU commands already available:

cargo build --release -p treams-cuda --features cuda --example benchmark_sampling
RAYON_NUM_THREADS=4 target/release/examples/benchmark_sampling 16384 512
python scripts/benchmark_sampling_blas.py 16384 512 --cuda

RAYON_NUM_THREADS=16 cargo run --release -p treams-cuda-tile \
  --features cuda-tile --example qualify_plane -- 1024 262144

Cached GPU sampling supports coefficient pullbacks; fused cuTile fields remain forward-only. Show cold setup/upload separately, and compare against the best matched CPU configuration.

items.html:
Actionable findings sent to the report agent:

  1. Cross-host evidence overwrite: both manifests use treams-comparison-v1; report filenames based only on that ID overwrite copied manifests/raw results. Use unique per-manifest storage keys.
  2. Confounded broad scaling curves: fractional Legendre workloads mix three degrees; internal illumination mixes one/eight columns; cylindrical fields use constant mode count while points vary. Split fixed parameters or reserve scaling plots for the explicit scaling plan.
  3. Misleading broad size metadata: firstbrillouin1d runs identical inputs despite varying --samples; other geometry workloads use radius rather than element count. Generic broad “dimension” curves should be omitted.
  4. Incorrect upstream recording label: the original harness marks both backends forward_records_adjoint=True for recorded workloads. Upstream never records; correct this in normalized reporting.
  5. Thread claims: Mac reports blas=[]; label budgets as requested rather than verified active BLAS threads. Parent confirmed Linux scaling will expose all 16 physical cores.

Read-only fingerprint check found all 29 completed Mac outputs consistent with the manifest’s native, Python, and harness hashes. No benchmarks, tests, builds, or source edits during this audit.

items.html:
All 21 illumination cases passed, with consistent source fingerprints; 19 include actual upstream comparisons.

  • N1024, L1, one illumination: native selected solves took 1.98 s versus upstream’s faster measured method at 43.79 s—22.1× faster. Matrix-free took 2.19 s, using 46.7 MiB versus 2463.5 MiB.
  • N16, L5, two illuminations: matrix-free achieved 103× faster fresh solves, with 4.54× lower peak RSS than upstream public full-T.
  • N4096: matrix-free completed in 35.14 s, using 57.4 MiB. This is native-only, weak coupling, dipole cutoff; no upstream speedup claim.
  • Losses: matrix-free is poor for cached reuse and many illuminations. At N128/P32 it was 1.44× slower than upstream and 47× slower than native selected.

Residuals, dense comparisons, Ward identities and radius-direction finite differences passed. Beyond the dense cap, zero comparison errors are self-comparisons, not independent validation.

Sent caption/methodology corrections to root/report agent. No code changes or numerical runs.
